events.subtitle: TJG George Wein Fellowship Commission 2026
events.category: Trumpet-led fellowship commission / new compositional project presentation
events.factual_description: The Jazz Gallery presents 2026 George Wein Fellowship artist Michael Rodriguez on Friday and Saturday, September 18-19, 2026, with sets at 19:00 and 21:00 each night. The venue identifies the engagement as 'TJG George Wein Fellowship Commission 2026 Presents - Michael Rodriguez.' The Jazz Gallery's fellowship program states that the award includes financial support, a two-week residency at the Pocantico Center, and year-long off-hours access to The Jazz Gallery so established artists can focus on new compositional projects. Rodriguez is a trumpeter and composer. The event page does not currently announce additional personnel or a title/program for the commissioned material, so no sidemen, repertoire, or premiere claim is inferred. The presenter lists general seating at $38.50, cabaret seating at $44, and livestream at $22, with member pricing also available; online pricing includes purchasing fees.

en.why_it_matters: This is not just another Michael Rodriguez club date. The Jazz Gallery's George Wein Fellowship is built to give established artists money, residency time, and physical space to develop new compositional work, and these two nights are the 2026 commission presentation. That puts Rodriguez's trumpet voice inside a process Listening Notes cares about: hearing an experienced improviser when the point of the engagement is new work rather than repertory maintenance. The missing details are also worth respecting—the presenter has not yet announced the full personnel or commission program, so the reason to care is the creation context itself.
en.trip_verdict: If September 18 or 19 already fits a New York trip, actively make room for one set and choose the night that best fits the rest of the itinerary. I would not build a dedicated DMV-to-New-York run around it until the commissioned program and any additional personnel are announced.

events.subtitle: Debut album release show
events.factual_description: The Jazz Gallery presents VEN Trio on Thursday, September 24, 2026, with sets at 19:00 and 21:00. The presenter explicitly bills the date as the album-release show for VEN Trio's debut album and verifies the collective as Vinicius Gomes on guitar, Elé Salif Howell on drums, and Noah Garabedian on bass. The Jazz Gallery describes the trio as centered on spontaneity, groove, a shared love of African music from the African diaspora, and genre-fluid experimentation. NYU's jazz program additionally describes Howell's VEN Trio project as blending Brazilian music, jazz, and indie influences through original compositions. The presenter lists general seating at $33, cabaret seating at $38.50, and livestream at $22, with member/student-member pricing also available; online pricing includes purchasing fees.

en.why_it_matters: VEN Trio puts three very different rhythmic instincts into a small frame: Vinicius Gomes's guitar language, Elé Howell's elastic drums, and Noah Garabedian's bass, with the band explicitly grounding the project in groove, spontaneity, African-diaspora music, and genre-fluid exchange. The debut-album release makes this date more useful than a routine club appearance because it catches the collective at the point where that shared language is becoming a recorded statement.
en.trip_verdict: If September 24 already puts you in New York, this is worth folding into the evening—especially if the Brazilian, groove, and instrumental threads are already part of the trip. I would not make it the sole reason for a corridor run from the DMV.

es.why_it_matters: VEN Trio mete tres impulsos rítmicos muy distintos en un formato pequeño: el lenguaje de guitarra de Vinicius Gomes, la batería elástica de Elé Howell y el bajo de Noah Garabedian, con el grupo situando explícitamente el proyecto en el groove, la espontaneidad, las músicas de la diáspora africana y el cruce de géneros. El lanzamiento del álbum debut vuelve esta fecha más útil que una aparición rutinaria de club porque captura al colectivo justo cuando ese lenguaje compartido se convierte en una declaración grabada.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 24 de septiembre ya te encuentra en Nueva York, vale integrarlo a la noche, especialmente si los hilos brasileño, de groove e identidad instrumental ya forman parte del viaje. No lo usaría como única razón para hacer un viaje por el corredor desde el DMV.
